newsitem.title: LATVIA: C.BANK SAYS INTEREST RATES TO STAY STABLE.
newsitem.headline: C.BANK SAYS INTEREST RATES TO STAY STABLE.

text.p: The central bank said on Wednesday that the conditions for succesful development of economy have been reached and that no further interest rates reductions its could be expected.
"The conditions for succesful economic development have been created...the banking crisis is securely behind us," Ilmar Rimshevics, central bank deputy president, told a news conference.
The bank has been gradually cutting rates and this month reduced its key refinanicng rate to four percent from five.
"We hope that this is the rate which will keep for a longer period. There are no grounds to think that this rate could go down further," Rimshevics said.
He said that interest rates have reached the level of more developed Western nations and a further fall was not justified.
"Interest rates in commercial banks have also reached their lowest levels, five to 5.5 percent," he said.
Rimshevics said the banking sector had gained funds needed for the development of the economy.
